title: Testing Robots
statementMd:
The Cybernetics Failures (CF) organisation made a prototype of a bomb technician robot. To find the possible problems it was decided to carry out a series of tests. At the beginning of each test the robot prototype will be placed in cell $(*x*_{0}, *y*_{0})$ of a rectangular squared field of size $*x* × *y*$, after that a mine will be installed into one of the squares of the field. It is supposed to conduct exactly $*x*·*y*$ tests, each time a mine is installed into a square that has never been used before. The starting cell of the robot always remains the same.

After placing the objects on the field the robot will have to run a sequence of commands given by string $*s*$, consisting only of characters '`L`', '`R`', '`U`', '`D`'. These commands tell the robot to move one square to the left, to the right, up or down, or stay idle if moving in the given direction is impossible. As soon as the robot fulfills all the sequence of commands, it will blow up due to a bug in the code. But if at some moment of time the robot is at the same square with the mine, it will also blow up, but not due to a bug in the code.

Moving to the left decreases coordinate $*y*$, and moving to the right increases it. Similarly, moving up decreases the $*x*$ coordinate, and moving down increases it.

The tests can go on for very long, so your task is to predict their results. For each $*k*$ from $0$ to $*length*(*s*)$ your task is to find in how many tests the robot will run exactly $*k*$ commands before it blows up.

## Input

The first line of the input contains four integers $*x*$, $*y*$, $*x*_{0}$, $*y*_{0}$ ($1 ≤ *x*, *y* ≤ 500, 1 ≤ *x*_{0} ≤ *x*, 1 ≤ *y*_{0} ≤ *y*$) — the sizes of the field and the starting coordinates of the robot. The coordinate axis $*X*$ is directed downwards and axis $*Y*$ is directed to the right.

The second line contains a sequence of commands $*s*$, which should be fulfilled by the robot. It has length from $1$ to $100 000$ characters and only consists of characters '`L`', '`R`', '`U`', '`D`'.

## Output

Print the sequence consisting of $(*length*(*s*) + 1)$ numbers. On the $*k*$-th position, starting with zero, print the number of tests where the robot will run exactly $*k*$ commands before it blows up.

## Note

In the first sample, if we exclude the probable impact of the mines, the robot's route will look like that: ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/16bfda1e4f41cc00665c31f0a1d754d68cd9b4ab.png).
statementZhMd:
CF（Cybernetics Failures）组织制作了一个炸弹处理机器人原型。为了找出可能存在的问题，他们决定进行一系列测试。在每次测试开始时，机器人原型会被放置在一个大小为 $*x* × *y*$ 的矩形方格区域中的 (*x*_{0}, *y*_{0}) 单元格内，随后会在区域中的某个方格内放置一枚地雷。计划总共进行恰好 $*x*·*y*$ 次测试，每次都将地雷放置在之前从未使用过的方格中。机器人的起始单元格始终保持不变。

在放置好这些物体后，机器人必须执行由字符串 $*s*$ 给出的一系列命令，该字符串只包含字符 '`L`'、'`R`'、'`U`'、'`D`'。这些命令分别指示机器人向左、向右、向上或向下移动一个方格；如果无法向指定方向移动，则机器人会停留在原地。当机器人完成全部命令序列时，它会因代码中的 bug 爆炸。但如果在某一时刻机器人与地雷处于同一个方格中，它也会爆炸，不过这次不是因为代码中的 bug。

向左移动会使坐标 $*y*$ 减小，向右移动会使其增大。同样地，向上移动会使坐标 $*x*$ 减小，向下移动会使其增大。

测试可能会持续很长时间，因此你的任务是预测测试结果。对于每个 $*k*$（从 $0$ 到 $*length*(*s*)$），请找出机器人在爆炸前恰好执行了 $*k*$ 条命令的测试次数。

## 输入格式

输入的第一行包含四个整数 $*x*$、$*y*$、$*x*_{0}$、$*y*_{0}$（$1 ≤ *x*, *y* ≤ 500, 1 ≤ *x*_{0} ≤ *x*, 1 ≤ *y*_{0} ≤ *y*$）——区域的大小以及机器人的起始坐标。坐标轴 $*X*$ 的正方向向下，坐标轴 $*Y*$ 的正方向向右。

输入的第二行包含一个机器人需要执行的命令序列 $*s*$。它的长度为 1 到 100 000 个字符，并且只包含字符 '`L`'、'`R`'、'`U`'、'`D`'。

## 输出格式

输出一个包含 $(*length*(*s*) + 1)$ 个数字的序列。第 $*k*$ 个位置（从零开始）输出机器人在爆炸前恰好执行了 $*k*$ 条命令的测试次数。

## 说明

在第一个样例中，如果不考虑可能与地雷发生碰撞的情况，机器人的移动路线如下所示：![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/16bfda1e4f41cc00665c31f0a1d754d68cd9b4ab.png)。
